thread:
sanjay: Quick kickoff — I want to propose we collapse the "PenaltyBuckets" heuristic into a single "ScoreComposer" primitive.

sanjay: Motivation: current bucket model duplicates logic (latency vs cost vs region) and makes hotfixes painful. Composer would let us express weighted scorers and fallbacks in one serializable contract.

maria: curious about migration. existing tenants depend on bucket semantics for preemption windows. how do we preserve behavior? :thinking:

sanjay: plan A: compatibility shim in policy-runtime that translates old bucket rules to an equivalent composer graph at loadtime. shim would emit warnings and increase trace detail.

ryan: +1 for shim but need to be careful with perf — composition graphs can be more expensive at eval time. do we have Q for eval cost?

amanda: we should add a lazily-evaluated matcher layer. only compute expensive parts when the fast-path selectors match. small cache for tenant-level compiled composers.

sanjay: agreed. idea: compile composer to a flattened list of scorers using heuristics we already have (region penalty, latency SLOs, cost-window). runtime would evaluate scorers in order and short-circuit when score threshold reached.

maria: can we see a proto sketch? would help for clients to understand serialization.

sanjay: here's a quick sketch:
```
message Scorer {
  oneof type {
    RegionPenalty region = 1;
    LatencySLO latency = 2;
    CostWindow cost = 3;
    Scripted scorer = 4; // for edge cases / legacy transforms
  }
  double weight = 10;
}

message Composer {
  repeated Scorer scorers = 1; // evaluated in order
  double short_circuit_threshold = 2; // stop when aggregated score >= x
}
```

ryan: that looks fine. questions: 1) numeric stability across quantized runtimes, 2) rule hotreload behavior, 3) telemetry labels for explainability.

amanda: for hotreload, keep both full-graph and a precomputed fingerprint. on change, we can diff fingerprints and apply canary if diff affects scoring order or weights.

maria: telemetry: please include per-scorer contrib and pre/post-score eviction counts. prod ops needs that to understand why a route was rejected.

sanjay: agreed — we'll add per-scorer tags and a trace hook. policy-bot: can you add a job to generate a migration checklist and a rough rollout plan?

policy-bot: Created ticket INF-1248: "ScoreComposer migration checklist". Assignees: @sanjay, @amanda. ETA draft: 2w. :white_check_mark:

ryan: implementation note — keep the evaluator in Rust runtime minimal: scorer enum -> function table. avoid dynamic dispatch through boxed closures in hot-path.

amanda: ops note — rollout strategy: 1) compile-only shim in dev against canary traffic 2) enable composer for non-critical tenants 3) full rollout with fallback to old bucket semantics per-tenant toggle.

maria: one more: how do we test parity? need deterministic test harness to compare old vs composer outputs over traffic replay.

sanjay: good point. add replay harness + property tests (idempotence of translation for a period). also add perf baseline before enabling.

amanda: I'll own the rollout doc and parity harness. ryan — can you own the runtime changes and perf testing?

ryan: yep. I'll spin up a prototype that compiles 10k tenant policies and measure eval p50/p99.

sanjay: thanks. action items captured:
- INF-1248 created (migration checklist) — policy-bot
- amanda: rollout doc + parity harness
- ryan: runtime prototype + perf numbers
- maria: telemetry schema for per-scorer contrib

sanjay: follow-up sync in 3 days to review prototype numbers. :thumbsup:
